subject: lion
pitch: A proud old lion resting with his head held high. A huge shaggy mane fading from golden blond at the face to dark chocolate at the edges, a tawny body with a pale cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, a broad black nose, a scar across one eyebrow, big padded paws and a long tail ending in a dark tuft.
reasoning:
I need to write a single compact TypeScript module, being careful about API correctness. I'm deciding on the lion's pose — considering a resting sphinx-like position with legs extended versus a simpler standing pose that might be safer to implement correctly in one pass.

I'll go with a lying sphinx pose, working out body dimensions and spine coordinates so the belly sits naturally against the ground, then building the skeleton with a root hip joint and chained spine, neck, and head joints using catmull-rom paths.

For the mane, I'm planning layered geometry with a radial colour gradient blending golden tones near the face into darker chocolate browns further out, likely using gradient-based colouring rather than raw paint functions since that's more reliable.

Computing mane lock positions in rings around a backward-facing axis from the neck, with each layer offset in radius and angle count to build a tufted, layered look.

Using spike cones for the mane layers, with roughly 100 total across five layers, plus an ellipsoid mass behind the head for volume—dark brown core with golden fringe at the face ring. Now I'm setting up the head joint and skull geometry at the neck end, oriented forward.

Working through the muzzle as a tapered box from the face outward, with a small black nose block near the tip, and defining the jaw joint and its own frustum shape beneath for the lower jaw...

Adding fangs, amber eye spheres with black pupils, brow ridges, and a scar detail across one eyebrow using a thin rod shape...

Working out exact head-local coordinates for the eyes and scar so they sit properly on the skull's curved surface, checking distances against the skull sphere radius and adjusting positions by hand since the math isn't lining up perfectly yet.

Good, forward 0.24 gets the eye right on the surface with radius 0.03 half buried. For the brow I'll add a small tawny box above it, then place a scarred rod diagonally across it from upper-outer to lower-inner, radius 0.007 in a dark reddish-brown tone.

I'll thicken that scar to 0.01 so it reads clearly even if partly buried. For ears, I'm placing small tawny spheres with darker inner coloring near the top sides of the head, accepting they'll be mostly tucked into the mane's front ring of cones but still poke through slightly at the right height and offset.

For the body, I'm planning to sweep a shape along the spine chain rather than modeling separately, using a radius function to vary the ellipse cross-section from deep chest to narrower hips, with the neck as its own sweep joining at the shoulders.

Still placing joints...

Defining the front legs now...

Now the tail: curling from the rump along the floor to the left side, with points curving outward and ending around length 1.2, tapering radius from 0.04 to 0.03. I'll chain it as a parented "tail" segment off the hips with 5 segments.

For the tuft, I'm adding a dark ellipsoid at the tail's end plus a ring of small cone spikes angled outward along the tangent for a bristled look, with the tail itself colored tawny and slightly darker near the tip.

Now I'm connecting the tail chain to the body, adjusting the rear cap position so the tail joins seamlessly around z=-0.9. I'm placing the hips joint and spine chain root, then sizing the hind thighs as scaled spheres positioned to fit within the body width, before starting on the neck path connecting from the chest to the head.

Setting up the neck chain parented to the spine's last joint, then defining the head joint attached to the neck's end, and now I'm building the jaw joint using local offsets from the head frame.

I'm placing the head at the neck's top, making sure the mane drapes naturally over the skull-to-chest connection, and now I'm settling on the color palette—tawny, cream, and gold tones.

Defining body sector colors...

I'm checking that downward-pointing cone tips don't poke through the floor or body, so I'm scaling the vertical direction and length for those cases to keep the spike bases and tips positioned correctly.

Now I'm working out the mane cone directions using a radial component plus a backward offset that grows with each layer, with elliptical stretching for the radius, and setting per-layer counts that increase from 12 to 24 (totaling 90 cones) with a slight angular offset alternation between layers.

Writing spike dimensions...

I'm defining a gold-to-dark-brown color gradient across the five layers, with each spike's color randomly blended between its own layer and the next for a more natural transition, and arranging the layers so inner ones sit toward the front while spikes point backward to keep the face visible, including a forehead fringe layer near the head joint.

Now I'm positioning the skull center slightly forward and sizing the inner mane ring so it frames the face like a lion's, with the ears placed using local offsets and small scaled spheres with darker inner coloring, checking that they fall within the mane ring's radius so they read as tucked into the fur rather than floating outside it.

Next I'm working out the facial details: cream whisker pads with tiny dark dots for whisker follicles, a chin tuft, and the muzzle shape built from a tapered box frustum that narrows toward the nose, placing the nose itself as a small rounded box at the front, and adding a tawny bridge slab across the top of the muzzle to blend into the face coloring.

Now I'm sorting out bone orientation — deciding to keep everything aligned to world axes rather than the head's local frame to avoid confusing rotations — then positioning the jaw as a tapered box running from the joint forward, sized and placed so its top edge meets the muzzle's underside for a closed-mouth look.

Adding dark thin rod lips along each side, then setting up amber eye spheres with smaller black pupil spheres offset slightly forward on the eye surface, elongated for shape.

Now placing small dark whisker spots on the muzzle surface and side rows, plus toe details on the paws and a hind leg sphere chain to flesh out the hind limbs.

Setting up the hind leg chain with hip, knee, hock, and toe points, then sweeping varying radii along it for a tapered leg shape, and doing the same for the front leg chain with its own radius taper.

I'm also planning shoulder and haunch spheres attached to spine bone joints for extra body volume, keeping the color scheme simple with plain tawny tones, and adding a dark tufted ellipsoid at the tail tip positioned using the tail chain's endpoint and tangent direction.

Adjusting tail tip height to .08 to avoid dipping below floor. Now adding a dark mane core ellipsoid behind the head, positioned slightly back and down, with brown fill to avoid gaps.

Settling on mane proportions with tiered spike radii and tilt, keeping the top around neck height so it reads as a huge shaggy mane without overwhelming the head. Now starting the actual builder export, defining the hips joint position.

Setting up the spine chain with a curved path from hips through chest, then sweeping the body profile with growing radii toward the chest and a flat-bottomed cross-section, applying the coat color with tawny sector mottling.

Still writing anatomy chains...
